title: Constant-tower direct image and limit normalization for identified ring sheaves
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with a specified ring isomorphism $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Module pullback $F=f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to module direct image $G=f_*$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ringed-topos convention [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$.
Let $\mathcal G=RG$ and $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}=R(G^{\rm Tow})$, with evaluation comparisons and $a_M:\mathcal G R\lim_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_Y\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$ normalized as in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\chi_K:\Delta_Y\mathcal G K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XK.$$
On a K-injective representative $J$ it is the equality $\Delta_YGJ=G^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XJ$. Under the normalized evaluation comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-tower-derived-evaluation-normalization], every evaluation of $\chi_K$ is the identity. The canonical maps $R\lim_T\Delta_TK\cong K$ of the strict-tower derived limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] identify $R\lim_Y(\chi_K)^{-1}a_{\Delta_XK}$ with $1_{\mathcal G K}$. The assertion applies to arbitrary ring sheaves $R_T$, not just constant coefficient rings. Under $F^{\rm Tow}\Delta_Y=\Delta_XF$, it also satisfies the strict counit equation $\varepsilon^{\rm Tow}_{\Delta_XK}\circ F^{\rm Tow}(\chi_K)=\Delta_X(\varepsilon_K)$.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim: diagram-topos proof, specialized to constant towers

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ and $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\mathcal A_T)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck] to the singleton category and to the inverse-sequence category: both $\mathcal A_T$ and $\mathcal T_T$ are Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] their complexes have K-injective resolutions. Kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal T_T$ are levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; thus the constant functor $\Delta_T$, evaluation $e_n$, and the levelwise functor $F^{\rm Tow}$ are exact (for the last use the exactness of $F$ in the setup). These exact functors descend termwise to derived categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. In particular $\Delta_TQJ=Q\Delta_TJ$ and $F^{\rm Tow}\Delta_Y=\Delta_XF$ with the specified termwise identifications.

The index category has terminal object $1$. A map of towers $u:M\to\Delta_T A$ is determined by $u_1:M_1\to A$: naturality forces $u_n=u_1\circ M(n\to1)$, and these formulas conversely define a tower map. Hence $e_1\dashv\Delta_T$, with $e_1$ exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to this adjunction shows that $\Delta_TJ$ is K-injective whenever $J$ is. This is an application of the existing exact-left-adjoint theorem, not an assertion that arbitrary diagrams of K-injectives are K-injective.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; explicit adjunction for the terminal index 1

proof.text: Since $F\dashv G$ and $F$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] gives that $H=GJ$ is K-injective for every K-injective $J$ on $X$. Step 2 then gives that both $\Delta_XJ$ and $\Delta_YH$ are K-injective. The underived equality $G^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XJ=\Delta_YGJ$ is equality of complexes of strict towers: all transitions on both sides are identities, and the differentials are $G(d_J)$. Therefore $J$ computes $\mathcal G$, $\Delta_XJ$ computes $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}$, and the resulting image complex is already K-injective, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived].

Write $\eta_G:QG\to\mathcal GQ$ and $\eta_{G^{\rm Tow}}:QG^{\rm Tow}\to\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}Q$ for the universal derived comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. For $K=QJ$ define
$$\chi_{QJ}=\eta_{G^{\rm Tow},\Delta_XJ}\circ(\Delta_Y\eta_{G,J})^{-1},$$
using $QG^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XJ=\Delta_YQGJ$. Both factors are invertible by step 3, so this gives the required representative-level isomorphism. Naturality of the two $\eta$'s gives naturality for chain maps between K-injective representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every derived map between such representatives is a unique homotopy class of chain maps and every quasi-isomorphism between them is a homotopy equivalence. Additive termwise functors preserve homotopies by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Consequently this formula descends to a natural isomorphism on the derived category and is independent of representatives: a change of representative conjugates the formula by those same naturality squares. No choice of an evaluated family of maps is used to construct $\chi$.

Let $\beta_n:e_n\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Ge_n$ be [lem-weil-pbc-tower-derived-evaluation-normalization]. Its stated normalization, applied to the K-injective tower $\Delta_XJ$, reads
$$\beta_{n,\Delta_XQJ}\circ e_n(\eta_{G^{\rm Tow},\Delta_XJ})=\eta_{G,J}.$$
Apply $e_n$ to the formula of step 4 and substitute this equation. Cancellation gives $\beta_{n,\Delta_XQJ}\circ e_n(\chi_{QJ})=1_{\mathcal GQJ}$, including the prescribed localization identifications. Thus every evaluation is the identity in exactly the normalization specified in the item. This is a calculation of the constructed morphism, not an inference of equality of tower-derived morphisms from evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, first proof: common direct-image composite on diagram topoi, specialized to constant towers

proof.text:
For an ordinary object $A$, a cone to $\Delta_TA$ is a family of maps all equal to its component at $1$; hence $\lim_T\Delta_TA=A$, with every projection the identity. Apply this degreewise to a K-injective $J$. Since $\Delta_TJ$ is K-injective by step 2, the K-injective model of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] and its total-derived comparison from [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] give a natural isomorphism
$$b_{T,QJ}:QJ=Q\lim_T\Delta_TJ\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_T\Delta_TQJ.$$
Its inverse $c_{T,K}$ is the canonical constant-tower limit identification in the statement. Explicitly $b$ is induced by the cone of identity maps $J\to J$ at every level. Its naturality and independence of representatives follow by the same K-injective Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] used in step 4. This proves the constant-limit identification rather than assuming it is an extra clause of the cited strict-limit node.

The comparison $a$ in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] is specified by deriving the equality $G\lim_X=\lim_YG^{\rm Tow}$. On $\Delta_XJ$, both derived composites are computed without any replacement: $\Delta_XJ$ is K-injective, $\lim_X\Delta_XJ=J$ is K-injective, and $G^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XJ=\Delta_YH$ is K-injective, by steps 2 and 3. The common underived composite on this object is the single complex $H=GJ$; its comparison with itself is $1_H$. The normalized derived comparison therefore gives, after inserting the $b$ of step 6 and the $\chi$ of step 4,
$$R\lim_Y(\chi_K)^{-1}\circ a_{\Delta_XK}\circ\mathcal G(b_{X,K})=b_{Y,\mathcal GK}.$$
Indeed each of these identifications, and $a$, is represented here by the equality $G\lim_X\Delta_XJ=GJ=\lim_Y\Delta_YGJ$. Compose on the left with $c_{Y,\mathcal GK}=b_{Y,\mathcal GK}^{-1}$. This is precisely the claimed identity after identifying the source by $\mathcal G(c_{X,K})$ and the target by $c_{Y,\mathcal GK}$.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, first proof: common direct-image composite on diagram topoi, specialized to constant towers

proof.text:
Finally compute the counits themselves. For a complex $B$ on $Y$ and K-injective $J$ on $X$, the Hom bijections [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and termwise adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_D(FQB,QJ)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(FB,J)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(B,GJ)=\operatorname{Hom}_D(QB,QGJ).$$
Here $FQB=QFB$ is justified by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and $GJ$ is K-injective by step 3. The transpose of $1_{GJ}$ under the middle bijection is the ordinary counit $\varepsilon^0_J:FGJ\to J$, so the canonical derived counit at $QJ$ is represented by that chain map. The same calculation in the tower categories is valid at $\Delta_XJ$, since $\Delta_XJ$ and $G^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XJ=\Delta_YGJ$ are K-injective. The ordinary tower adjunction is obtained by taking the ordinary mates at each level; naturality of the ordinary unit and counit ensures these mates commute with transitions. Its counit at $\Delta_XJ$ is thus exactly $\Delta_X(\varepsilon^0_J)$ as a map of complexes of strict towers. Under $F^{\rm Tow}\Delta_Y=\Delta_XF$, $\chi_{QJ}$ is the identity identification of those representatives by step 4. Therefore
$$\varepsilon^{\rm Tow}_{\Delta_XK}\circ F^{\rm Tow}(\chi_K)=\Delta_X(\varepsilon_K)$$
in the derived category of strict towers, by localization of the equality of these chain maps. Naturality extends this to every $K$.

Checks: (1) the diagram categories for J=pt and N>=1^op are Grothendieck for any ring sheaf, and levelwise exactness makes Delta, e_n and F^Tow exact; (2) e_1 -| Delta checked by hand (u_n = u_1 o M(n->1)), and right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective applies with u=Delta, v=e_1; (3) G preserves K-injectives because F is exact, and G^Tow Delta_X J = Delta_Y GJ holds strictly; (4) chi = eta_{G^Tow} o (Delta_Y eta_G)^{-1} has the right types, is invertible, and extends to D through the K-injective Hom bijection; (5) the beta normalization at Delta_X J gives e_n(chi)=1; (6) lim Delta J = J, and b is invertible by K-injectivity; (7) a, being the common-composite comparison, is represented by 1_{GJ} because all three inputs are K-injective, and the equation's types check; (8) both counits are represented by eps^0_J and Delta_X eps^0_J, and the tower equation is the localization of an equality of chain maps, not an inference from evaluations.
